content:
“The Wife” actor received an Honorary Academy Award on Nov. 15, following eight Oscar nominations without a win.

Close, 79, said during her acceptance speech that it was “very difficult for me to process this incredible honor” because she carries “the epigenome of an outsider.”

“From the ages of 7 to 22, I was under the thumb of a restrictive cult,” she said, referencing her family’s time in the group formerly known as Moral Re-Armament.

“‘Don’t look at yourself in the mirror. No flirting. Dress this way. Talk this way. Say it’s OK when your parents are routinely sent away from you for months on end,’” she said. “It meant that I was always looking on the outside ― I was always on the outside looking in.”

“In 1970, I found the strength to leave the cult and enrolled as a 22-year-old freshman at the College of William and Mary,” she said, explaining that she “went straight to the theater department, auditioned, and ended up getting cast as Olivia in Shakespeare’s 12th Night.”

Her career took off from there, as Close went on to star in hits like “Fatal Attraction,” “Dangerous Liaisons,” “101 Dalmatians” and “The Wife.”

And even though she was nominated for eight Academy Awards over the last four decades, Close said that because she felt like an outsider, she “never worried about whether I was going to win or not, though some years I thought I might have a chance.”

Close grew emotional over the course of her speech and ended by dedicating her win to her only child, Annie Starke.

“There’s one person who never asked to be the daughter of an actor, a celebrity, but who has navigated those challenging waters with wisdom, humor, ferocity and love,” Close said. “My daughter, Annie, who when she was three, looked up at me and said, ‘I want you. I want all of you.’”

“Being a working single mother, I knew exactly what she meant, but I also knew it was something I couldn’t always promise her,” Close added. “You are my heart and soul. I share this with you, my darling girl. And to Mark, her husband, and my grandson, Rory. The pain of leaving is always relieved by the joy of coming home. I love you beyond measure. What I do will always be for us.”

The now-Oscar winning actor has spoken about her time in Moral Re-Armament before, which started when her father, who was a surgeon, moved his family from Connecticut to Switzerland to follow the group’s founder, minister Frank Buchman.

Close told The Guardian in 2025 that she endured “a kind of psychological abuse couched in underlying misogyny.”

“It never leaves you. It’s insane that what happens at a certain time in your childhood is right here,” she said, tapping her chest.
